newsitem.title: UK: Ofreg partly accepts MMC N.Ireland Elec plan.
newsitem.headline: Ofreg partly accepts MMC N.Ireland Elec plan.

text.p: The Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) on Friday published its report on Northern Ireland Electricity's (NIE) pricing review, which regulator Ofreg has only partially accepted.
"My present intention is to largely accept the Commission's proposed modifications," said Ofreg's director general Douglas McIldoon.

The MMC in its report proposed that the revenues allowed by the price control formula should be reduced to 25 percent in 1997/98 compared with 1996/97, and cut by two percent in real terms in each of the four subsequent years.
Regional electricity company (Rec) NIE had proposed a cut of 22 percent, while Ofreg had sought a 31 percent reduction.

The MMC said on the basis of its assessments the price control for the next five years should be set to give NIE total revenues from its transmission and distribution business with a net present value of 575 million stg at 1996/97 prices.
But McIldoon said: "I am not...currently minded to accept the modifications proposed by the commission for NIE's transmission and distribution without an adjustment".
McIldoon said that the MMC recommendation is based on assigning a particular value to the asset base of NIE's transmission and distribution (T&D) business, but he disagrees on two issues.
The MMC's recommendation is set by applying an "uplift" to the opening day valuation of NIE. McIldoon disagrees on the need for the need to apply "uplift" to the valuation.
He also does not accept the MMC's proposed change to the company's depreciation policy for pre-flotation assets on which NIE earns a return under the price control.

McIldoon said he had "difficulty" accepting the MMC's recommendation for the level of capital expenditure and operating expenditure for NIE's T&D business. He said he is prepared to allow the MMC's proposed levels for 1997/98 and 1998/99, but had asked NIE to submit to him the corporate plan on which the MMC recommendation is determined.

"The effect of varying the Commission's recommendations in respect of uplift and depreciation only, and accepting their recommendations in respect of operating and capital expenditure, would be to set a price control which would allow NIE to recover revenues with an NPV of 555 million stg," said McIldoon.
He added the effect on domestic electricity prices on this basis would be a reduction in real terms of 15 percent between 1996/97 and 1997/98, compared with the commission's estimate of 14 percent.

The MMC concluded in its summary report: "The reductions are a little lower than those which would have resulted from implementation of the DG's proposals, but greater than those implied by NIE's counter-proposals".
On March 13, NIE announced it was cutting prices for domestic customers by at least 8.0 percent from April 1 and making smaller cuts for bigger industrial and commercial customers.
